v.rationale: Both use the same correct concurrency design: lock the coupon row in a transaction, then check per user and against the cap, with a unique index as backstop. Both fire the event after commit and return correct 201/200/404/409 codes, and both suites pass. impl-2 wins because it fires CouponRedeemed inside the domain method, so the exactly-once rule holds for every caller. impl-1 fires it in the controller, and a probe showed that calling redeemFor directly fires no event. impl-1's 409 exception also has an empty message. impl-2 also uses slightly better idioms (whereBelongsTo, throw_if with a class-string, an explicit factory default). impl-1 has a nicer route group and a sequential cap test. Neither has a true concurrent-request test.
